list: geometry-only inventory (third list of the held-out test, step 3 of 7)
drawing: presidential suite_layout.dwg (Revit export, 3D team, 9 Nov 2026); floor tag suite_revit; drawing metres = DXF mm / 1000
format: keys/tower/labels/inventory-l29.json: a list; this header is the first element and has no floor, a or b; every other element is one opening with floor 'suite_revit'. Kinds ending in '?' are uncertain kinds; 'optional': true marks entries not to be scored either way.
method: Worked from the geometry only, without any picture: no PNG was opened (neither keys/suite_revit/pictures/ nor any rendering of my own). Read description.md, drawing.json and layer_roles_from_description.json for orientation, the tower inventory / labeller lists, the bank key's part notes (curtain-wall convention only) and tools/score.py for the format and the conventions. Then, with scripts in labels/work_C/ (cache prims.pkl and the DXF through ezdxf): (1) every INSERT (124: 6 door blocks, 18 curtain panels, 42 mullions, 6 columns, 1 Walls 13 block, casework, furniture); (2) every ARC in model space and in the inserts (2,078) with exact centre, radius and angles, the swing-like ones flagged (r 0.28-2 m, sweep 15-125 deg): 20 on A-DOOR / A-DOOR-HDLN are door swings, the other 31 are bed linen (A-GENM), furniture and table rims (I-FURN) and a fridge door (Q-SPCQ); (3) all 200 fill polygons on layer 0, A-WALL, S-COLS and A-GLAZ-CWMG with size, thickness and direction; (4) all 282 A-DOOR / A-DOOR-FRAM line segments clustered by place (27 clusters: every one belongs to a listed door); (5) the wall solid W = union of the wall fills (less two furniture fills, two specks and the shower's 10 mm glass pane) and, from each end of every fill piece at least 40 mm thick, a march along its axis in a band of 60 % of its thickness: skip material that continues the wall, then measure the stretch with no material up to 3.5 m (55 gaps; run again letting the wall continue through other pieces first: 93 in all, 41 of them new; every one judged: openings kept, room interiors, corridor crossings and corner artefacts rejected); the same march listed the wall ends with no material within 3.5 m (open sides); (6) A-WALL and layer-0 lines that do not lie on the fill boundary (walls drawn without fill, lines across openings, glass screens, casework): no wall without fill except the two 10 mm glass screens with their 0.10 m kerb lines; (7) the curtain-wall panes, each marched along its glass line to the A-WALL pieces at both ends; (8) the door, panel and window block definitions, used or not (the suite's doors were exploded: their unused definitions DOOR_SWING_1_SOLID - 800 / - D09, DOOR_SWING_DOUBLE_TYPE 2 - L16_D07, DOOR_SLIDING_CAVITY_1_SOLID - D13, IN_SHOWER DOOR1 and Doors 1 match the exploded doors; no window family, no window layer); (9) a check of every entry: material just beyond both ends (sampled across the wall), no wall fill between them.
conventions: Ends a and b on the wall centre line at the faces of the wall ends (the ends of the wall fills; the 50 mm A-DOOR-FRAM frames stand inside the gap, so the clear width is 0.10 m less: 1.10 vs 1.00 for the pocket doors, 0.80 vs 0.70 for the 0.70 leaves, 1.00 vs 0.90). A door at a corner ends at the face of the cross wall. A door in a glass screen is measured by its leaf (= the gap in the glass). Doors outside the suite (corridor service doors to risers, two unit doors of neighbouring units) are doors in walls of the drawing and are listed. Optional: shower-enclosure doors (the conventions leave out shower screens), the two doors cut by the view crop (width not readable), open sides and recess mouths (passage mouths into open space), and the fixed curtain-wall glazing of the six bays (no opening sash; the bank key made such glazing in a facade gap optional). Not listed: casework, cupboards, wardrobes, furniture, the fixed glass of the screens.

uncertain.what: C-24 (glass door of the master-bathroom WC compartment): scored as the door of an enclosed WC compartment (WC drawn at x 10.32-10.69, y 6.79-6.92), but it is the same exploded shower-door family (IN_SHOWER DOOR1 - Shower door_700X2160MM) as the three optional glass doors; if the key treats it like a toilet cubicle door it becomes optional.

C-28: Glass door in the screen of the unnamed room east of the BOH: optional as a shower door (shower-door family, kerbed screen like the master shower), but nothing is drawn in the compartment behind it (x 22.89-24.80, y 3.42-4.72) except a 0.97 x 0.35 m box against its south wall (bench?). If it is a WC compartment it should be scored like the master-bathroom WC door.

C-38: Bi-fold door of the walk-in wardrobe (2.225 m): scored as a room door (a gap in a real partition, a walk-in room behind it). If the key reads a walk-in wardrobe as a cupboard it would become optional.

C-44 and C-36: The two D22 service double doors at x 23.99-25.79 (y 1.1591 and 3.2591) are cut by the view crop at x 25.0785: ends given from the family (1.80 m, symmetric about the insert point); only 1.092 m is drawn. Optional both.

C-32: Door of the small room south of the foyer: 0.75 m between the wall fills, but the 0.80 m family frame (return 554C) starts 0.05 m inside the 0.10 m wall stub on the hinge side; the clear leaf is 0.70. Used the fills (0.75).

Widths: every door is measured wall end to wall end with the frames; a list measuring the clear opening between the frames will be exactly 0.10 m narrower on the exploded suite doors, which is at the scorer's width limit (10 cm or 10 %).

Curtain-wall bays listed per facet (18 optional windows), as each facet is a straight glazed run between solid A-WALL pieces (wall ends, Walls 13 corner wedges). The alternative reading, one bay = one gap of the facade line (e.g. x 3.85-7.38 on y 11.41-11.51 for bay N1, x 2.81 between y 2.93 and 8.79 for the west bay), is not listed.

C-27: BOH door from the bar: the two wall pieces differ in thickness (0.175 / 0.20 m); the centre line is taken on the core x 20.5116 (frame lines x 20.4366-20.5866). Same for C-21 (x 20.5116), C-22 (x 22.8116), C-16 / C-37 (x 7.4539).

C-31 and C-20: The open north side of the dressing area and the open north side of the lobby of bedroom 2 are listed as optional passage mouths: each is a wall end with nothing in line on the far side (the partition there holds a pocket door at that height).

C-17 and C-19: the two doors of the master shower (x 9.57-11.49, y 7.07-10.23) are optional as shower-enclosure doors; they are real hinged glass doors in a glass partition, so a key that scores doors in glass partitions regardless of use would score them (and C-28).

C-40 and C-43 (recess mouths, optional) lie 0.30 m in front of the unit doors C-41 / C-42, exactly the scorer's 0.30 m centre tolerance for a 1.0 m door: a passage detected at a mouth could be paired with the door.

rejected.reason: 0.80 m gap x 13.8866-14.6866 in the 0.20 m shaft wall y 1.0091-1.2091 (A-WALL 540F): the fire-hose cabinet block FHC 02 - Type 1 (M-EQPM, 0.80 x 0.35 m, text FHC) fills it: a recessed cabinet, not an opening.

Luggage-rack niche x 20.6116-20.7866, y 7.7766-8.4766 in the 0.175 m lining on the bedroom-2 side of the partition x 20.41-20.61 (A-WALL rounded returns 58C5-58C8, Q-CASE slatted rack inside); the partition behind is continuous.
Box x 22.90-23.87, y 3.42-3.77 at the south-west corner of the room east of the BOH (single layer-0 lines A625 / A626, beside the riser wall 4DF9): a 0.35 m recess or bench, no gap in a wall.

Empty void x 15.11-15.51, y 3.78-5.06 between the foyer and the bar's west wall, closed on the foyer side by the single layer-0 line 62B0 (x 15.1116): closed void or full-height cupboard; the 1.28 m between the A-WALL jamb 540C (ends y 3.7841 with its lining) and the L-wall arm (y 5.0607) is no doorway (no leaf, frame, head or threshold).
Corridor bay x 17.14-20.44, y 3.31-3.66: the corridor's north wall steps back 0.35 m between A-WALL 540D and the partition 51BE; a wall jog, not an opening.
Bar / living and dining: open plan with no wall line (bar counter and back counter are casework).
Fixed glass: the shower's north pane (fill 4DEB, x 9.5116-11.4966, y 10.2291-10.2391) and the fixed glass of both screens: glass walls / shower screens.

Casework and furniture: master-bedroom wardrobe along the south wall (x 3.29-7.35, y 0.33-0.96, dashed division lines 50F2 / 50F3), dressing counter, walk-in wardrobe shelving and island, bedroom-foyer cabinet (x 7.55-8.00, y 3.47-4.92), lobby wardrobe (y 5.43-6.03), TV wall unit (x 11.64-12.01), bar counters, BOH counter, shelving along the angled facade walls; swing-like arcs of bed linen (A-GENM), table rims and furniture (I-FURN), the fridge door (Q-SPCQ arc r 0.5 at (22.0616, 3.4841)): not openings.
The risers behind the four service doors (X marks on A-DETL and layer 0) and the closed shaft x 12.01-14.69, y 0.41-1.01: no further opening.
March lines through the spaces south of the corridor (x 14.89-15.89 and x 17.14-23.89 at y 0.66-0.76): outside the corridor behind continuous corridor walls; not openings.

March artefacts: wall ends facing a wall across a room or the corridor (e.g. the WC / shower wall end at the screen to the bathroom's west partition, 1.92 m; the BOH north wall line across the room east of the BOH), corner pieces of the bays (0.25-0.35 m between stubs and wedges), a 7.5 mm sliver at x 7.544-7.551 and slivers above two columns.
Bay mouths on the facade line (one per bay): where the room runs on into the projecting curtain-wall bay; the glazing is listed per facet instead (see uncertain).
